title: Normalized exchange and geometric-fibre identification of the zero-section compact class
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_F$ with uniformizer $\varpi_F$, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $\pi:E\to B$ a rank-one vector bundle with zero section $z$ [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]. For the Cartier divisor $D=z(B)$ let $c_{D,A}:z_*A_B\to A_E(1)[2]$ be [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map], with the prescribed twist of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Define $\tau_E=R\pi_!c_{D,A}:A_B\to R\pi_!A_E(1)[2]$ using the identity-normalized source comparison for $\pi z=\mathrm{id}_B$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition].

For any morphism of $k$-schemes $g:B'\to B$, let $E'=E\times_BB'$, $v:E'\to E$, $\pi':E'\to B'$ and $z':B'\to E'$ be the pullbacks. Use a compactification of $\pi$ and its pullback to define the compact-support functors on $B'$ if $B'$ is not finite type over $k$. Let $C_{\pi,g}:g^{-1}R\pi_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi'_!v^{-1}$ be the finite-level pro-etale exchange of [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale], and use the canonical supported-constant and twist pullback comparisons. Under the corresponding source identifications the exchange on $R\pi_!z_*A_B$ is the identity of $A_{B'}$, and the actual morphisms satisfy
$$C_{\pi,g}(A_E(1)[2])\circ g^{-1}\tau_E=\tau_{E'},$$
where $\tau_{E'}=R\pi'_!c_{z'(B'),A}$ uses the pulled-back source identification. No flatness assumption on $g$ is made.

In particular let $\bar b:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$ be a geometric point, where $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, and choose a basis of the fibre line identifying $(E_{\bar b},z_{\bar b})$ with $(X,0)$ for $X=\mathbf A^1_\Omega$. The canonical compact-fibre comparison [lem-pur-cfiber-stalk], applied to the finite-Tor object $A_E(1)[2]$, identifies the geometric-stalk morphism of $\tau_E$ with the pro-etale realization of
$$\tau_X^e:A\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},L_X[2]),\qquad L_X=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{\ell^n,X}\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z/\ell^n}A,$$
the ordinary etale compact image of the supported Kummer morphism of $0\subset X$. The realization uses [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] over the field $\Omega$ and the projection-induced identification $\nu_X^*L_X\cong A_X(1)$. Thus this comparison identifies the morphism as well as its target object; no supported-cohomology group is identified with compact cohomology by this assertion.

source.place: Step 3: base-change compatibility, and Step 2 first paragraph: identify the geometric-fibre morphism; previous expanded proof steps 3--4

proof.text: Check the pulled-back pair. On a trivializing affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ the bundle and section are $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$ and $V(t)$. After any affine base change $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to U$ these are $\operatorname{Spec}R'[t]$ and $V(t)$. Multiplication by $t$ is injective, since the coefficient of $t^{i+1}$ in $t\sum a_it^i$ is $a_i$. Thus $D'=z'(B')$ is Cartier even for nonflat $g$. This argument is local on both bases and so covers arbitrary $B'$. The augmentation $t\mapsto0$ and projection still compose to the identity. These are the zero-section data of [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section].

source.place: Step 3, checking the Cartier hypothesis for arbitrary pullback

proof.text: Put $K=A_E(1)[2]$ and $M=z_*A_B$. Since $\ell$ is a unit times $\varpi_F^e$ with $e\geq1$, $\ell^nA=0$. Apply [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] with annihilating exponent $r=n$. It supplies an ordinary etale supported morphism $c^e: Rz_*A_B\to L_E[2]$ whose pro-etale realization is $c=c_{D,A}$, where $L_E=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{\ell^n,E}\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z/\ell^n}A$. The same statement identifies the pullback of $c$ with $c'=c_{D',A}$ using the supported-constant and prescribed-twist comparisons; Step 1 checks its only extra geometric hypothesis. On the etale side [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] supplies the same supported morphism and its pullback identity. Finite direct image is exact by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]; the module version follows because forgetting scalar action commutes with underived direct image and detects exact sequences. Thus $Rz_*=z_*$ here. On the pro-etale side [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] gives this equality: the zero-section complement is quasi-compact locally, since it is $D(t)\subset\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$. The primed assertions follow by the same local calculation.

source.place: Step 3, supported Kummer pullback; Cartier source construction detailed in lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map.proof.md

proof.text:
Compute the source comparison on a compactification $E\xrightarrow j\bar E\xrightarrow pB$. Let $s=jz$; since $ps=1_B$ and $p$ is separated, [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion] makes $s$ closed. Both $z$ and $s$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Apply [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] to the square with top open $1_B$, bottom open $j$, left proper map $z$ and right proper map $s$. It gives $j_!Rz_*\cong Rs_*$. Therefore, using the normalized direct-image comparison of [lem-cbc-etale-derived-direct-image-coherence],
$$R\pi_!^eRz_*A_B=Rp_*j_!Rz_*A_B\cong Rp_*Rs_*A_B\cong R(ps)_*A_B\cong A_B.$$
All maps used are the normalized proper/open and direct-image maps, so this is the compactification construction of the source comparison in [thm-sf-comp-composition], with $\pi z=1$. The primed comparison is computed by the pulled-back diagram. Its construction uses only the given proper/open model; it makes sense for arbitrary $B'$ and invokes no finite-type-over-$k$ theorem on $B'$.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; blueprint Step 3

proof.text: The source exchange is the identity, not just an automorphism of a rank-one object. Work first on the ordinary etale models. The last displayed base-change equation of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence], for the square in Step 3, identifies exchange on $Rp_*j_!Rz_*A_B$ with the successive proper exchanges for $p$ and $s$ on $A_B$. The exchange is the specified unit--square--counit map of [def-cbc-exchange-map]. Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies these successive exchanges, under the direct-image compositors of [lem-cbc-etale-derived-direct-image-coherence], with exchange for $ps=1_B$. Part (4) says this mate is the identity. Thus under the comparisons of Step 3 the source exchange is $1_{A_{B'}}$. For the pro-etale functors use [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]: its exchange is exactly this etale exchange transported through the proper/open and pullback comparisons. On the original diagram these comparisons identify the source normalization by [lem-sp-finite-compact-site-coherence], including its identity and composition equations: the proper comparison is the counit-normalized mate of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], the open comparison is [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], and part (2) of the mate-pasting lemma identifies their proper composite for $ps$ with the identity comparison. All original schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (a field has only two ideals). On arbitrary $B'$, use the transported source comparison of the pulled-back proper/open model stipulated in the statement, not a new application of the Noetherian coherence theorem. The transported identity is therefore $1_{A_{B'}}$.

proof.text:
Write $a:A_B\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi_!M$ and $a':A_{B'}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi'_!M'$ for the inverse source comparisons, and $\beta:v^{-1}M\xrightarrow{\sim}M'=z'_*A_{B'}$. Step 4 says $R\pi'_!(\beta)C_{\pi,g}(M)g^{-1}a=a'$. Step 2 gives $c$ the etale witness $c^e$. The etale exchange is natural in its argument by [thm-cbc-finite-torsion], and the exchange of [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] is that etale exchange transported through the natural proper/open and pullback comparisons and conjugated by the witness isomorphisms, independently of the witness. Hence, applied to $c:M\to K$, it is natural:
$$C_{\pi,g}(K)g^{-1}(R\pi_!c)=R\pi'_!(v^{-1}c)C_{\pi,g}(M).$$
Step 2 gives $v^{-1}c=c'\beta$ after the target twist comparison. Compose the displayed equality with $g^{-1}a$, and substitute the source equality. Its right side becomes $R\pi'_!(c')a'=\tau_{E'}$ and its left side is $C_{\pi,g}(K)g^{-1}\tau_E$. This proves the equality of the actual morphisms for every $g$, with exactly the source identification in the statement.

source.place: Step 3, explicit naturality square and its source normalization

proof.text: The input $K=A_E(1)[2]$ satisfies the finite-Tor hypothesis of [lem-pur-cfiber-stalk]. Indeed [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](3)--(4) makes $A_E(1)$ a finite locally constant, locally free rank-one sheaf. Tensoring locally with it is tensoring with $A$, so it is exact. Hence $K\otimes_A^LM$ is concentrated in degree $-2$ for any sheaf $M$; this is the interval $[-2,-2]$ in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Apply [lem-pur-cfiber-stalk] at $\bar b$. Its canonical comparison is the compact-fibre exchange, so Step 5 with $g=\bar b$ identifies the stalk morphism of $\tau_E$ with the compact image of $c_{D_{\bar b},A}$. The chosen fibre basis carries $D_{\bar b}$ to $0\subset X=\mathbf A^1_\Omega$. Apply [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] to this isomorphism of Cartier pairs: the supported morphism becomes $c_{0,A}$ with the same prescribed twist.

source.place: Step 2, first paragraph: finite-Tor compact-fibre comparison and the class of the origin

proof.text:
Finally [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] makes $\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{\ell^n,X}$ locally free over $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$, so the derived tensor defining $L_X$ agrees with its ordinary tensor. The root projection comparison [lem-amb-tate-root-projection-reduction], with $r=n$, and [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] identify $
u_X^*L_X$ with the prescribed $A_X(1)$ and identify $
u_X^*c^e_{0,A}$ with $c_{0,A}$. Apply [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] over the field $\Omega$ to $X	o\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and the morphism $c^e_{0,A}$. Both schemes and the compactification are finite type over $\Omega$, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], even when $\Omega$ is not finite type over $k$. Naturality in the witness identifies its compact image with $
u_\Omega^*(R\Gamma_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},c^e_{0,A}))$. On the source supported at the origin the comparison is the identity-normalized one: compute with the closed section in a compactification as in Steps 3--4, and use the counit normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] and the composition rule of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Thus the source is $A$, and the resulting morphism is precisely the realization of $	au_X^e$. This proves the asserted identification of morphisms; no assertion equating supported cohomology and compact cohomology has been used.

Properness of the closed zero section and its compactified section, for the proper/open square.
Formal pasting and identity of actual adjunction mates, used to normalize source exchange; no purity computation is replaced.
Etale finite direct image is exact, so supported constant sheaves equal their derived direct images.
Counit normalization of site-comparison direct image, required to identify the source map rather than an unspecified isomorphism.

Its identity and composition equations identify the etale/pro-etale source normalizations on the original Noetherian diagram and the Noetherian fibre diagram. It is not applied to an arbitrary non-Noetherian base change.
Verifies the Noetherian hypothesis of the generic compact-support site coherence theorem over k and over Omega.
